name: Pale Orange-Yellow
lede: Pale Orange-Yellow is a light, warm yellow tipped with orange, a descriptive name more than a historical one.

sections.title: A description, not a history
sections.body:
The name describes a position between [[yellow]] and [[orange]], lightened [3]. It is listed in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and in Ridgway's 1912 color book [3].

The books we hold have no passage about this color as a name. The only match, in Gurney, is a list of pale orange and yellow among the colors of a film's color script, which treats them as two separate colors [1]. We leave it there rather than invent a history [1]. Close neighbors include [[cream]] and [[light-yellow]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #FED590, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pale Orange-Yellow is one of the more common pale colors in our archive, found in 356 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.5 percent, as photographed [2]. It is commoner than 69 percent of the named colors, and peaks in the 1500s, found in 23 of the 2,231 paintings from that century [2].
